answer.title: The network where you own your identity
answer.text: SimpleX is the only messaging network without user identifiers. Nobody can contact you, or pretend to be somebody you know, unless you give them a link. You join without a phone number or an account. What would you like to do?

answer.title: Infrastructure for all communications
answer.text: SimpleX is the only messaging network without user identifiers. It has 600,000+ monthly users, 20x more than at our 2023 round, and 200+ people have invested on Wefunder so far. We plan to earn from businesses and big channels, while private messaging stays free. What would you like to know first?

answer.title: A private place for your family
answer.text: On SimpleX nobody can reach your family, or pretend to be one of you, unless one of you gives them a link. Everyone joins without a phone number, on iPhone or Android, and private messaging is free. Where would you like to start?

image.alt: A group of people joined in one private chat

answer.title: An audience that stays yours
answer.text: You hold the keys to your channel, so no platform can take it from you, and your readers stay private. What would you like to do?

image.alt: A channel sending posts to its readers

options.label: Run a community by my rules

answer.title: One link, a private chat with each customer
answer.text: Give your customers one link, and each of them gets a private chat with you. You answer from your phone or your team's server, and a bot can answer first. The line runs on your own keys and you pay nothing per message, so no platform sits between you and your customers.

image.alt: A public address that customers open to start a private chat

answer.title: How fast is it growing?
answer.text: 600,000+ people use SimpleX every month, up 70% in six months and 20x organically since our 2023 round. People found it through more than 200 reviews, posts and videos in over 20 languages, and the app has been downloaded over 3 million times.

answer.title: How will it make money?
answer.text: We have no user data to sell, so private messaging stays free and shows no ads. We plan to earn from those who want to be found or need more capacity: businesses and channels buy names, businesses pay for website chat, and big channels pay for servers. Supporter badges are on sale now.

answer.title: What do I get if I invest?
answer.text: Every investor receives a supporter badge, from one month at $100 to a year as a legend at $10,000. From $500 you also receive a public SimpleX name: 8 or more letters from $500, 7 from $1,000 and 6 from $5,000. It is registered for 5 years while early bird terms apply, and for 3 years after that. Invest before December 10 to reserve yours ahead of the public sale.

answer.title: Bring everyone at once
answer.text: You create a group, name it Family and send its link through any app you already use. Each person installs SimpleX, opens the link and joins when your phone is online. You can let each person in yourself, and you can delete the link when everyone has joined.

answer.title: Get my parents on it
answer.text: Your parents need one link from you, and then they can write to you and call you. Nobody else can reach them unless a link is shared with that person, so their chat list holds only the people they know. The app works in 26 languages on Android and 17 on iPhone, and the text can be made larger.

answer.title: Is it safer than WhatsApp?
answer.text: WhatsApp and Signal encrypt your messages, and Telegram does this only in secret chats that you start yourself. All three register you with a phone number, so your safety rests on a company's promise about what that account reveals, and a breach or a change of owner can end a promise. SimpleX registers nobody, so the protection is part of how the network is built. These apps are ahead today on linked devices, backups and group calls.

answer.title: Start a channel today
answer.text: Open the app, choose Create public channel, add a name and a picture, and share the link. Chat relays forward your posts from the first day, and you can add contributors who post with you.

answer.title: Keep my Telegram channel safe
answer.text: Keep your Telegram channel and open a SimpleX channel beside it. You share the link with your readers, and those who join remain with you if Telegram blocks the channel. You post to both by hand.

options.label: How does it compare with Telegram?

answer.title: Run a community by my rules
answer.text: You set the rules of your group, from who joins and who posts to what remains. Members can talk to admins privately and report problems, and the largest listed group has more than 9,000 members.

answer.title: Start today
answer.text: You can start now. Make a profile for your business in the app, turn on Business address and write a welcome message. Share the link or the QR code, and each customer gets a separate chat with you. For now your customers need the SimpleX app.

options.label: Get a name customers can find

answer.title: Let AI answer first
answer.text: A bot can answer first and bring in a person when the customer asks. SimpleX's own line works this way. The customer chooses the AI, the AI answers from a file the team wrote, and the first reply from the team ends it. You run the bot yourself, so you pay your AI provider and nobody else for each answer.

answer.title: Answer as a team
answer.text: On your own, you answer in the app and can add colleagues to any customer chat. With a larger team, your line runs on your own server, each new chat appears as a card in your team's group, and anyone on the team can join it with one tap. The customer sees who is answering. Today a developer sets this up.

answer.title: Do people stay?
answer.text: About one monthly user in five opens SimpleX every day, up from 17% to 21% in the six months to June, and about one in four in the US and Germany. Public groups in our directory hold over 160,000 memberships. Telegram channels tried to migrate in 2024/25, before SimpleX channels could scale.

options.label: What do I get if I invest?

answer.title: Why now?
answer.text: If an AI can copy your voice and your face and fake your phone number, a phone number proves nothing. On SimpleX nobody can contact you or pretend to be somebody you know unless you give them a link. AI also makes surveillance of private life and deplatforming cheap, so more people want a network that keeps no record of who they talk to.

answer.title: What do names earn?
answer.text: A public name lets people find a channel or a business without a long link, and only the owner's key controls it. Names will go on sale at an expected average price of $50 a year. At that average, 10,000 names would cover our operating cost of about $360,000 a year. In 2022 Telegram sold over $50 million of usernames in about four weeks, with far more users than we have.

options.label: What do I get if I invest?

answer.title: Why can't others copy it?
answer.text: Other networks are built on user identifiers, so they would have to rebuild from scratch to remove them, and the big ones earn from those identifiers. Their privacy is a promise that lasts until the company is compromised. Ours is in the architecture: we hold no list of who talks to whom, so there is nothing that can be breached or sold. A newcomer would need users, creators, businesses, developers and servers all at once, and SimpleX already has them.

answer.title: Who is behind it?
answer.text: Evgeny Poberezkin designed SimpleX. He led engineering at MailOnline and Stream, and he created Ajv, a JavaScript library with over 1.5 billion downloads a month. The team is five people, three of them here since the start, and everyone ships code with AI tools. All of this was built on $1.7M of investment.

answer.title: How do I invest?
answer.text: You invest on Wefunder, a regulated funding portal, from $100. You create an account, confirm your identity, choose an amount and pay by card, bank transfer or wire. Wefunder adds a payment fee, and it shows the fee before you confirm. People outside the US can invest too, if the law of their country allows it.

options.label: What do I reveal by investing?

answer.title: What can a name do for me?
answer.text: A name opens your channel or your address, as #example or @example.simplex, in place of a long link. You can point it at your own address so that people find you by name, or keep it for a channel or a business you start later. You control it with your own key.

answer.title: What do I reveal by investing?
answer.text: Investing is the one place where a real name is needed. Wefunder must verify who you are and asks for a tax ID, and we receive investors' details for legal and tax records. None of this touches your SimpleX chats or your contacts, because the network has no user identifiers to link it to.

answer.title: Move our WhatsApp group
answer.text: A family can move at its own pace. You post the link to your new Family group in your WhatsApp group, and people join when they are ready while the old group keeps working. Old messages stay in WhatsApp.

answer.title: What can we do together?
answer.text: You can write, send voice messages of up to five minutes, send photos, videos and files of up to 1 GB, and call each other one to one by audio or video. Groups have replies, mentions and reactions, and you choose how each chat notifies you.

answer.title: Make it easy for them
answer.text: You can make the text larger, give each person a name your parents recognize and put the family in a list of its own. You can do all of this for them when you install the app on their phone.

answer.title: Keep scammers away from them
answer.text: SimpleX uses no phone numbers and holds no directory of people, so a stranger has nothing to look up. Someone can reach you only through a link you gave them or a group you are both in, and a request through your address waits until you accept it.

answer.title: Who can see my messages?
answer.text: Only the people in a conversation can read it. Messages are end-to-end encrypted and padded to one size, so a server can neither read them nor measure them. A server sees random addresses and the times of messages. With private routing, on by default, the server your contact chose does not see your IP address. Your internet provider sees which servers you connect to.

answer.title: What does it cost?
answer.text: Private messaging stays free, and the app shows no ads. SimpleX Chat plans to earn from public names, business messaging and servers for big channels, and users have donated over $650,000 so far. If you want larger files and longer storage, you can buy a supporter badge.

answer.title: Put my channel on my website
answer.text: Your channel can appear on your own website. The app gives you a short piece of code, you paste it into your page, and visitors see your recent posts and a Join button before they install anything.

answer.title: Get a name for my channel or business
answer.text: A name lets people find you without a long link. #example opens your channel, and @example.simplex opens your business address. You control it with your own key, so no server can take it away, and if your link stops working you can point the name to a new one. Invest $500 or more before December 10 to reserve one ahead of the public sale.

image.alt: A public name on a SimpleX profile

answer.title: Can anyone shut me down?
answer.text: Your channel's keys are on your devices, so no operator can take it from you. Chat relays forward your posts. If a relay stops forwarding them, you add another relay or run your own, and your link, your name and your subscribers remain the same.

answer.title: What do my readers get?
answer.text: A reader opens your link and taps Join. Your recent posts and new ones then arrive like messages, and the reader can react to them. Other subscribers cannot see who is reading, and the servers cannot connect one channel a person reads to another.

answer.title: How does it compare with Telegram?
answer.text: You keep your audience, your rules and your readers' privacy. Telegram and Discord are ahead today on scheduling, pins, statistics, comments, voice rooms and paid subscriptions.

answer.title: Keep spam and abuse out
answer.text: You can delete any message, block a member for everyone, remove people with their messages, review each newcomer and make trusted members moderators. Members report problems to your moderators privately, and groups listed in SimpleX Directory can add a captcha and reject offensive member names.

answer.title: Grow past thousands of members
answer.text: Channels are built for any number of subscribers, because relays forward each post and subscribers never connect to each other. Groups run peer-to-peer, and the largest listed group has more than 9,000 members.

answer.title: Bring my customers over
answer.text: You can keep WhatsApp or Telegram while customers move at their own pace. Put your link in your profile, your messages and your receipts. Each customer who opens it gets a private chat with you, and you pay nothing per message there.

answer.title: What does it cost?
answer.text: Private messaging, groups, channels, a business address and the support bot are free. A supporter badge costs $7 a month, and a public name is expected to cost $50 a year on average. You pay your AI provider yourself, and we charge nothing per seat or answered chat.

answer.title: Who can read these chats?
answer.text: Messages are end-to-end encrypted between your customer and you, and servers hold no profiles or contact lists. You read what your customer writes and you keep it, so it is yours to protect. If you use an AI provider, it reads what the bot sends it.

answer.title: What does AI change?
answer.text: Each new kind of computer has needed a new network: the internet for mainframes, the web for PCs, app stores for smartphones. AI models are the next kind of computer, and people already work with them in chat. Those who use AI agents need what SimpleX provides: an identity no platform controls and communication no one can observe. SimpleX may become that network, and our company plans to earn from it without owning it.

answer.title: Has anyone checked this?
answer.text: Trail of Bits audited SimpleX in 2022, 2024 and 2026, and the last report will be published soon. The code is open source, the servers and the Android and Linux apps can be rebuilt from it, and independent reviewers such as Privacy Guides recommend SimpleX. We publish every request for user data in our transparency reports.

answer.title: What could go wrong?
answer.text: This is an early company with almost no revenue, and you could lose all the money you invest. Growth can slow, and you may not be able to sell for a long time. Please read the risks on Wefunder too, and ask us your questions there.

answer.title: What are the terms?
answer.text: The terms of this round are on Wefunder: what you receive, the price and the dates. We keep them in that one place, because Wefunder is the regulated home of this round. Please read them before you invest. If anything is unclear, ask on the Wefunder page, and we answer there in public.

answer.title: Check it is really them
answer.text: Anyone can copy a name and a picture, so a profile can't tell you who is writing. The keys are part of the link you share, so servers cannot replace them. To check that nobody replaced the link on the way, compare your security code in person or in a call, and the app then marks the contact as verified.

answer.title: Why not stay on WhatsApp?
answer.text: On WhatsApp and similar apps, the platform holds your number or account, sets the price of each message and can restrict you. On SimpleX your line is a set of keys on your device, and your address sits on servers you choose, including your own if you run one. If you move your address, the customers you already talk to stay connected.

answer.title: How could I make a return?
answer.text: You benefit if the company grows. From today's point of view, the most likely routes to a return are an IPO or a sale to other investors. Our goals for the next two years are to launch revenue, reach 1–2 million monthly users, cover our costs and raise the next round. You may not be able to sell before then, or for longer.
